blocks.text: The ancient naturalists regarded corals as stones and placed them among the minerals. Later ones considered them a plant, and this is the view of Rashi both in our Talmud passage and in the Bible passage cited above. Only at the beginning of the last century did Peyssonel discover the animal nature of this zoophyte, which is why we believed we ought not to omit this article.

Ἐνίους γὰρ αὐτῶν ἕως μὲν τοῦ στήθους καὶ τῶν ἐμπροσθίων ποδῶν διατετυπῶσθαι καὶ κίνησιν λαμβάνειν, τὸ δὲ λοιπὸν τοῦ σώματος ἔχειν ἀδιατύπωτον, μενούσης ἔτι κατὰ φύσιν τῆς βώλου. [Enious gar autōn heōs men tou stēthous kai tōn emprosthiōn podōn diatetypōsthai kai kinēsin lambanein, to de loipon tou sōmatos echein adiatypōton, menousēs eti kata physin tēs bōlou.]

Ἀκούω δὲ ἐν τῇ Θηβαΐδι χαλάζης πεσούσης ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὁρᾶσθαι μῦς, ὧν τὸ μὲν πηλός ἐστιν ἔτι, τὸ δὲ σάρξ ἤδη. [Akouō de en tȩ̄ Thēbaïdi chalazēs pesousēs epi tēs gēs horasthai mys, hōn to men pēlos estin eti, to de sarx ēdē.]

Ὅπου γε περὶ Θήβας τὰς Αἰγυπτίας ἐπειδὰν ὕσῃ ἐν καύμασι, εὐθὺς ἀρουραίων μυῶν ἡ χώρα ἀποπληροῦται. [Hopou ge peri Thēbas tas Aigyptias epeidan hysȩ̄ en kaumasi, euthys arouraiōn myōn hē chōra apoplēroutai.]

Harduin relates at this passage from his own experience: Et nos animalcula vidimus e ligno putri pariter inchoata, jam parte corporis viventia, novissima earum parte adhuc lignea sensus experte, one more proof of the possibility of the existence of our zoophyte.

The exact determination of the colour of the pearl is even decisive in matters of religious law, see Nidda 41b שתי טיפי מרגליות etc. From our passage in Joma it follows that ברלה is identical with מרגליות, since the Bible (Num. 11, 7) makes the manna equal in colour to the בדלח; see, however, Rashi on the Bible passage and Winer (R.-W. s.v. Bedellium).
